info.title: Postrail API
info.description: Send application email through your own Gmail or Outlook mailboxes, and sign your users in with Google, an emailed link or an emailed code. `/v1` takes API keys; `/app` is the dashboard and takes the session cookie. Errors always have the shape `{ error: { code, message } }`.

post.summary: Swap a redirect code for a user and a session
post.description: Finishes an OAuth or magic-link sign-in. Codes are single use. Returns the session token, which is never shown again, and a short-lived access token (a JWT) you can verify without calling Postrail.

post.description: Answers `active: false` for an expired, revoked or unknown token; that is not an error. For checks on every request, verify the access token against the JWKS instead.

200.description: Whether the session is live, and whose it is

post.summary: Get a fresh access token for a session
post.description: Call this when the access token is about to expire. A session that was revoked or expired answers `active: false` and no token, which is how sign-out reaches a tenant that verifies offline.

200.description: A new access token, or `active: false`

post.description: Freezes the template and the list as they are now, then sends as fast as the mailboxes allow. A broadcast uses at most 80% of each mailbox’s daily limit, so a large list is spread over several days and application email keeps flowing. Suppressed addresses are skipped, and every email carries an unsubscribe link.
